cards.explanation: The answer is no rain yet and no man to work the ground. Verse 5 gives two reasons: the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground. Two things missing, and the field is just waiting, friends. It's like a mixer with no dough and nobody to turn it on. Plenty of potential and zero cookies.

The answer is springs welling up from the earth. Verse 6 says springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground. No rain, no problem, bakers. The water came up from below instead of down from above, and that's a plot twist I did not see coming.

The answer is dust, friends! Verse 7 says the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground. Think about that for a second. I spent years under dust in a junk drawer and never once became anything but dusty.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says the LORD God breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being. The breath came from God Himself, bakers. That's where the man's life starts.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says that out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. Pretty to look at and good to eat, friends. That's a garden doing its job.

The answer is to cultivate and keep it. Verse 15 says the LORD God placed the man in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it. The man has real work to do from the start, bakers. A job with a purpose beats a Monday with nothing on the calendar, if you ask me.
The answer is False. The LORD God says, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden…” (Genesis 2:16). That's a whole garden of yes, friends. Only one tree gets a no, and that comes in verse 17.

The answer is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The LORD God says, “…but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil…” (Genesis 2:17). Out of a whole garden of trees, one gets that warning, bakers. Verse 9 puts that tree in the middle of the garden, along with the tree of life. Everything else is open, because the LORD God also says, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden…” (Genesis 2:16).

The answer is True. The LORD God says, “for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.” It's a clear warning, friends, and it comes with the command. I think a warning like that is a serious thing to hear.

The answer is for the man to be alone. The LORD God says, “It is not good for the man to be alone.” Think about it, bakers. The garden has trees pleasing to the eye and a river watering it, and the one thing the LORD God points to is that the man is by himself.

The answer is helper, friends! The LORD God says, “I will make for him a suitable helper.” Notice the word suitable. It's not just any helper, it's one who fits. That's like the right lid for the right canister.

The answer is to see what he would name each one. Verse 19 says the LORD God brought the beasts and the birds to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name, bakers. I would still be stuck on the first one, changing my mind.

The answer is False. The man named all the livestock, the birds of the air, and every beast of the field. But verse 20 says that for Adam no suitable helper was found. A whole parade, friends, and not one match.

The answer is one of his ribs, bakers! Verse 21 says that while the man slept, the LORD God took one of the man's ribs and closed up the area with flesh. The man was in a deep sleep the whole time. I think that's one sleep nobody could complain about.

The answer is woman, friends! Verse 22 says that from the rib the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him. The rib comes first, and then the woman is brought to the man. That's the answer to the helper the LORD God promised.
The answer is because she was taken out of man. The man says, “she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.” He gives the reason himself, bakers. The name fits where she came from.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 24 says, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife…” It's the same thing the text says. The reason it points back to is what just happened with the man and the woman.
